newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African shares finished off highs, failing to react positively to a better June producer price inflation and dragged lower by De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's results which dealers described as "dissapointing."
Tax payable by De Beers and its international arm De Beers Centenary AG was $156 million in the interim period compared to $105 million in the same period last year.
"The bottom line earnings may not be as high as expected, but principally because of a higher rate of tax," Des Mayers, diamond analyst at O'Flaherty, Sundelson & Co told Reuters.

Market watchers were dissapointed when stocks failed to react positively to a better-than expected producer price index figure. June PPI was up 7.5 percent year-on-year or down 0.2 percent month-on-month from 8.4 and 0.9 percent in May.
Economists had forecast PPI rising 8.3 percent year-on-year or 0.5 percent month-on-month in June.
"The market eased off after the PPI figure much to our surprise," one dealer commented.
However, dealers said the main economic indicator to watch was the July credit extension figure due later this month which would hopefully reinforce continued expectations of an interest rate cut.
They said some futures play has also been seen, adding to intraday volatility. In addition, nervousness on Wall Street hit the market in the afternoon.
Gold shares finished flat on a dull bullion price.
The overall index ended off 3.2 points at 7,579.9 points, the industrial index finished up 28.3 points at 9,267.7 points and the gold index rose 0.8 points to 1,017.1.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declining issues by 215 to 157, with 157 issues unchanged. Turnover was 970 million rand.

Chemicals firm Sentrachem added 55 cents to a new year high of 10.80 as jobbers bought stock on expectations U.S. chemical giant Dow Chemical Co would better its buy offer after Setrachem rejected an initial one.
NBS saw a large bookover of 500,000 shares which boosted turnover to 68 million rand. The share was last up 25 cents at 100 rand.
South African early equity futures ended steady to weaker on profit taking. Dealers said there was also some nervousness about Wall Street's prospects.
The market was expected to look to Wall Street and the gold price for direction on Wednesday.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,678/82 from 8,682, the all-share contract was at 6,748/67 from 6,753 and the gold contract was at 722/25 from 721.
